case_title: A Kattukulangara Madhavan (Dead) thr. LRs v. Majeed & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Political rival (members of opposing political parties); no personal relationship described
statutory_provisions: IPC s.143, s.147, s.148, s.341, s.323, s.302 r/w s.149 (charged); finally s.326 r/w s.149 for convicted accused
weapon: Knife (MO.1) used by one accused for stab wounds; sticks and a reaper used by others
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PW3, PW4); medical evidence (post-mortem certificate and stab injury findings)
aggravating_circumstances: Death from multiple injuries, including a stab wound to the left chest cavity; attack linked to political rivalry
mitigating_circumstances: Incident occurred in 1993; other accused caused simple injuries on non-vital parts with sticks
trial_court_outcome: Convicted A1, A2, A4, A14, A15, A18 under s.302 r/w s.149 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment; acquitted A5-A13, A16, A17
high_court_outcome: Acquitted A3, A14, A15, A18 of s.302/149; altered A4's conviction to s.324/149 with 1 year; upheld acquittal of A5-A13, A16, A17
offence_finally_established: Grievous hurt under IPC s.326 r/w s.149 (A3, A4, A14, A15, A18)
neutral_facts: On the evening of 10 March 1993, a group gathered at a road junction where an opposing political party had a presence, searching for supporters of that party travelling in passing buses. The victim was travelling in a stage carriage bus that stopped at the junction. Several persons boarded the bus, pulled the victim out, and took him to the front of the bus, where he was attacked. One of the attackers inflicted a stab wound on the back of the left side of the victim's chest and then two more stab wounds. When the victim tried to stand up, the other attackers beat him with a reaper and sticks. The victim was later found unconscious and bleeding on the road margin and was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. The informant's statement was recorded at midnight and a first information report was registered. The autopsy recorded 26 injuries, with the cause of death given as multiple injuries to the chest. A stab wound of about 7.5 cm entered the left chest cavity and was stated to be sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death. An independent resident who was travelling in the same bus described the attack, and another resident who lived nearby gave evidence naming further participants. A knife was identified in evidence. The informant, another eyewitness and the bus driver turned hostile, and several attesting witnesses to the seizure also turned hostile.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple injuries (26 injuries), including stab wounds to the chest; other attackers caused simple injuries on non-vital parts
number_of_offences: 6 charged; 1 finally upheld (s.326 r/w s.149 IPC, for five convicted accused)
premeditation_planning: Not found as planned murder; court found the assembly gathered and searched for rival party workers in buses, and rejected the High Court's view that absence of plan to murder negated common object
motive: Political rivalry between opposing parties (accepted by the Court)
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness PW3 (independent, vivid account, naming stab attackers); eyewitness PW4 (named A3, A14, A15, A18 and their involvement); post-mortem and stab injury findings; identified knife
witness_credibility: PW3 independent and believed by both lower courts; PW4 believed by Trial Court and should not have been limited to corroboration; PW5 and PW6 disbelieved by lower courts
trial_duration: offence: 10.03.1993; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 05.09.2005; Supreme Court: 30.03.2017
legal_representation: For accused: Siddharth Luthra, Sr. Adv. (with others). For complainant/appellant: Basant R., Sr. Adv. For State of Kerala: G. Prakash, Advocate
investigation_status: FIR registered (FIR No. 95 of 1993); investigation considered perfunctory by complainant, who filed a private complaint
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Supreme Court; High Court rejected defence objection to unexplained FIR delay and delayed reaching Magistrate
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted six under s.302/149 (life), acquitted others. High Court: acquitted A3, A14, A15, A18 of s.302/149; A4 reduced to s.324/149 (1 year); acquittals of others upheld. Supreme Court: appeals of complainant and State allowed in part; A3, A4, A14, A15, A18 convicted under s.326/149 (7 years); other acquittals upheld
prosecution_argument: High Court erred in discarding PW5 and in limiting PW4 to corroboration; common object was proved; all accused liable under s.302/149 IPC
defence_argument: PW3, PW4 and PW6 were interested partisan witnesses; no independent eyewitness; conduct unnatural; benefit of doubt due; mere presence without overt act not inculpatory (A4)
legal_principle_applied: Common object under s.149 inferred from nature of assembly, arms and conduct; mere presence may vicariously fasten liability; presence suggests participation unless conduct shows dissociation
precedent_relied_upon: Lalji v. State of U.P. (1989) 1 SCC 437; State of UP v. Dan Singh (1997) 3 SCC 747; Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade v. State of Maharashtra (1973) 2 SCC 793
sentencing_rationale: Incident occurred in 1993 and the accused attacked with sticks causing simple injuries on non-vital parts; s.326/149 conviction meets the ends of justice; 7 years imprisonment
judicial_mitigating_factors: Lapse of time since 1993 incident; simple injuries on non-vital parts caused by sticks
other_sentence_order: A3, A4, A14, A15, A18 to surrender within 4 weeks to serve sentence
